page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-highcpu-4 is a compute-optimized instance built on x86_64 architecture using a 2.3 GHz Intel Xeon 8581C processor. It provides 4 virtual CPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, paired with 8.0 GB of system memory, giving 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and vector/matrix instructions including AVX-512 and AMX tile processing. The instance includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, no integrated GPUs, and no default local storage.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-core performance alongside trade-offs in memory bandwidth. The c4n-highcpu-4 achieved top-tier Geekbench single-core scores and strong single-threaded performance in gzip compression, bzip3 decompression, and text processing. Conversely, multi-core CPU stress tests and uncached memory bandwidth read/write speeds measured in lower benchmark brackets. Software compilation via Clang and extended PassMark memory tests also recorded lower performance categories.

From a cost-efficiency and hardware density perspective, the c4n-highcpu-4 provides dedicated vCPUs with a lower memory-to-core ratio, prioritizing raw single-thread execution over high-capacity memory operations. Workloads suited for this server include static web serving, Redis caching operations, light LLM prompt processing, text processing, and single-threaded batch execution.
